news.text: 8 June saw the **1990 FIFA World Cup (Italia '90)** kick off at the San Siro in Milan with one of the greatest shocks in football history: unfancied **Cameroon**, led by 38-year-old supersub Roger Milla, stunned defending champions Argentina 1–0 despite finishing the match with nine men. The tournament captured global imaginations with Luciano Pavarotti singing *Nessun dorma*, defensive masterclasses, and an intoxicating Italian summer atmosphere.
news.youtube: Cameroon vs Argentina World Cup 1990 opening match

news.text: 1 June saw Paul Verhoeven's sci-fi action thriller ***Total Recall***, loosely adapted from Philip K. Dick's story *We Can Remember It for You Wholesale*, explode into cinemas. Starring **Arnold Schwarzenegger** as construction worker Douglas Quaid discovering his memory has been artificially wiped and Sharon Stone as his lethal double-agent wife, the $65 million spectacle delivered jaw-dropping practical mutant effects, Martian shootouts, and mind-bending reality twists, grossing over $261 million.
news.youtube: Total Recall 1990 theatrical trailer Arnold Schwarzenegger

news.text: 9 June saw synth-pop pioneers **New Order** secure their first and only UK number one single with the official England World Cup anthem ***World in Motion***. Co-written with comedian Keith Allen and featuring an unforgettable mid-song rap delivered with swagger by England winger **John Barnes** (**"You've got to hold and give, but do it at the right time"**), the track dethroned traditional terrace novelty anthems and soundtracked England's heroic run to the semi-finals.
news.youtube: New Order World in Motion official video John Barnes rap 1990

news.text: 1 June saw US President George H. W. Bush and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev sign the historic **Chemical Weapons Accord** during a high-stakes summit in Washington D.C. The bilateral treaty committed both superpowers to halt all production of chemical weapons immediately and systematically destroy at least 80% of their existing chemical munitions stockpiles, marking a monumental step toward dismantling Cold War arsenals.
news.youtube: Bush Gorbachev chemical weapons treaty Washington 1990

news.text: 23 June saw **Elton John** reach number one on the UK Singles Chart with his double A-side release ***Sacrifice / Healing Hands***. Championed by BBC Radio 1 DJ Steve Wright, the poignant ballad stayed atop the British charts for five consecutive weeks, giving the music legend his very first solo UK number-one single after more than two decades of international chart-topping success.

gaming.title: Super Mario Bros. 3 (Western Release)
gaming.reviewQuote: The greatest 8-bit platformer ever built. Overflowing with secrets, Raccoon suits, and pure unadulterated joy.
gaming.headline: Batmania for Mario: The Golden Age of NES Platforming
gaming.gameplay: Promoted relentlessly across the West through the Hollywood movie *The Wizard* (where Fred Savage's character famously unveiled it in a tournament), *Super Mario Bros. 3* arrived on Western NES consoles in mid-1990. Directed by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka, the game introduced the world to **Raccoon Mario** (taking flight with a swishing tail), Frog Suits, Tanooki Suits, and eight massive themed worlds (including the surreal Giant Land) navigated via an interactive overhead map.
gaming.reception: Releasing across North America and Europe throughout mid-1990, *Super Mario Bros. 3* sparked absolute retail hysteria. Department stores sold out instantly, with delivery trucks under armed watch. *Mean Machines* awarded it an astonishing 98%, calling it the finest platformer ever constructed on any system, praising its responsive inertia, immaculate secrets, and Koji Kondo's timeless musical score.
gaming.impact: Selling over **17 million copies**, *Super Mario Bros. 3* generated over $500 million in revenue, surpassing the box office hauls of contemporary Hollywood blockbusters and cementing Mario as the undisputed king of popular entertainment at the dawn of the 1990s.
